summary: Okanogan County, WA summit site: an L-4 cab dated 1940 was removed or destroyed in 1950, and one researcher doubts a structure ever stood there.

facts.design: L-4 cab, dated 1940 in the register
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1950, per the sources. Willhite doubts a lookout structure ever stood on the summit.

visit.trail_note: Wikipedia says there is a summit register and that talus can make climbing difficult.

events.note: L-4 cab dated 1940 in the register and firelookout.com; Willhite reports the same through the Kresek Inventory but doubts a structure ever stood
Register says the L-4 cab was removed in 1950
firelookout.com and Willhite (citing the Kresek Inventory) say the cab was destroyed in 1950
Registered November 18, 2012; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: site is 15 miles WSW of Twisp

evidence.quote: Built in 1940, this L-4 cab was removed in 1950.

evidence.supports: Kresek Inventory lists 1940 L-4 cab destroyed 1950 (Willhite citing)
evidence.quote: The Kresek Inventory lists Oval Peak as having an L-4 cab in 1940 that was destroyed in 1950.

evidence.supports: Willhite has found no map or trail showing a lookout on the summit
evidence.quote: I have not found one map showing a lookout or a trail to the top of Oval Peak.

evidence.supports: Willhite doubts the structure was ever there
evidence.quote: I am suspect of the structure ever being there

evidence.supports: register names the Okanogan National Forest
peak protected by the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness within the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Wikipedia)
evidence.quote: It is protected by the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness within the Okanogan–Wenatchee National Forest
There is a summit register at the peak.
Climbing Oval Peak can be difficult due to the amount of talus on its slopes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed in 1950; firelookout.com and Willhite say it was destroyed that year. Willhite also doubts a structure ever stood there. The story reports all three.
The register says Okanogan National Forest; Wikipedia says Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. The story reports both names.

notes_for_editor: The brief lists kind 'ground'. No source I read says whether the L-4 cab stood on a tower or on the ground, so I left that value alone for the editor to check. Willhite's doubt that any structure stood here makes this the weakest of the three records. No source states access, so access is omitted. The 2012 registration date and the 8,798 ft elevation match the brief.
